body.statement: Let \(N=nm\), \(d=|\mathcal G_n|\), and order cells by \(o\). Under the inference assumptions, \((X_{k,g},\mathbb G_k)_{k=1}^N\) is a \(d\)-dimensional martingale-difference array, \(N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^NE_P[\lVert X_k\rVert_\infty^3]=O(1)\le N^{1/8}\), and polynomial family growth implies \(\log^{7/2}d=o(N^{1/4})\), which is Belloni and Oliveira's growth inequality with \(\delta_N=N^{-1/16}\) and \(\varrho=1/8\). Matrix Freedman concentration gives \(\max_{g,g'}|N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^N\{X_{k,g}X_{k,g'}-E_P[X_{k,g}X_{k,g'}\mid\mathbb G_{k-1}]\}|=o_P(N^{-1/8}\log^{-2}(eNd))\). Deterministic leave-one-cell-out rank \(r\) approximation then gives \(\max_{g,g'\in\mathcal G_n}|(s_gs_{g'})^{-1}\sum_{i,j}g_{ij}g'_{ij}\widehat e_{ij}^2-\Omega_{gg'}|=o_P(\log^{-2}(enm d))\) and \(N^{-1}\max_{g\in\mathcal G_n}\sum_{k=1}^N(\widehat X_{k,g}-X_{k,g})^2=o_P(N^{-1/8}\log^{-2}(eNd))\). Consequently \(\max_g|\widehat s_g/s_g-1|=o_P(\log^{-2}(eNd))\) and \(P(\min_g\widehat s_g\ge\tfrac12\sqrt{c_s}B/\sqrt{N})\to1\). These conclusions use no independence claim for the leave-one-cell-out fits.
body.justification: This discharges the increment, dimension-growth, empirical-covariance, residual-consistency, and positive-studentizer obligations instead of assuming feasible bootstrap validity.
body.gap: Belloni and Oliveira's Assumption 2 and Theorem 3.3 begin with normalized martingale increments and a plug-in increment approximation; they do not derive those objects from adaptive low-rank causal scores.
body.consumer: It provides a checkable audit trail for simultaneous HeartSteps II contrasts and prevents saturated-rank residual collapse.
